questions.q: The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi></math> of pure water at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>80</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is
questions.solution:
At 25°C, the value of the ionic product of water is10-14. The ionic product of water is defined as 

Kw=H+OH-⇒10-14=H+OH-For pure water H+=OH-So H+=10-7Thus the pH=7

Since the degree of ionization is proportional to temperature, the value of the ionic product of water increases with increase in temperature. So, the ionic product will increase at a temperature more than 25°C
Therefore, at 80°C, the ionic product will increase and so the hydrogen ion concentration will increase and thus, the pH will become less than 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following does not form a buffer solution?
questions.solution:
A buffer solution is formed when we have a mixture of a weak acid or base and its corresponding salt with a strong base or acid.
A $1: 1$ mixture of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ will have unequal concentrations of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}$ so it will not act as a buffer.

questions.q:
Match the following

  List-I   List-II
(A) Aq. Solution of AlCl3 (I) Basic
(B) Aq. solution of CH3COONa (II) Acidic
(C) Aq. solution of KCl (III) Highly conductive
(D) Al2O3 (IV) Strongly basic
    (V) Amphoteric

The correct match is
questions.solution:
AlCl3 is a salt of weak base and strong acid, it undergoes cationic hydrolysis

Al+3+3H2O→Al(OH)3+3H+

H+ ions are released in to the solution.Hence, the aqueous solution of AlCl3  turns acidic in nature.

Aqueous solution of CH3COONa undergoes anionic hydrolysis as it is a salt of weak acid and strong base and the solution will basic in nature due to the release of OH- ions.

CH3COO-+H2O→CH3COOH+OH-

Al2O3 is amphoteric in nature as it reacts with both acids and bases.

Aqueous solution of KCl  is highly conductive in nature as KCl is an ionic compound.

Hence, the correct match is 

  List-I   List-II
(A) Aq. Solution of AlCl3   Acidic
(B) Aq. solution of CH3COONa   Basic
(C) Aq. solution of KCl   Highly conductive
(D) Al2O3   Amphoteric

questions.q: If the molar concentrations of base and its conjugate acid are same, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pOH</mi></math> of the buffer solution is
questions.solution:
According to the buffer solution the pOH of solution is :-

pOH=pKb + logSaltbase

If the molar concentrations of base and its conjugate acid are same then Salt=Base

So, the pOH=pKb + log1=pKb+0=pKb

Hence, if the molar concentrations of base and its conjugate acid are same, then pOH of the buffer solution is same as pKb of base.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The $\mathrm{pH}$ of the solution, when
(i) sodium acetate is dissolved in water.
(ii) ammonium chloride is dissolved in water.
questions.solution:
$\because$ (i) Sodium acetate, i.e. $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}\right)$ in water gives $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and $\mathrm{NaOH}$ as follows :
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COONa}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}+\mathrm{NaOH}$
Hence, for $(\mathrm{i}) \mathrm{pH}\gt 7$. $\quad[\because$ solution is basic $]$ 
Also,
(ii) when, ammonium chloride, i.e. $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}\right)$ is added in water, it gives $\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}$(aqueous) and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ (aqueous) ions.
$\mathrm{NH}_4^{+} \text {(aqueous) }+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{OH}^{-}$
Hence, $\mathrm{pH} \lt  7$
Hence, the correct answer is, for (i) $\mathrm{pH}\gt 7$ and for (ii) $\mathrm{pH} \lt  7$.

questions.q: Calculate the molar solubility of calcium hydroxide $\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2$ in $0.10 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaOH}$ solution. The ionic product of calcium hydroxide is $5.5 \times 10^{-6}$.
questions.solution:
Given,
Ionic product of $\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2=5.5 \times 10^{-6}$
Concentration of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution $=0.10 \mathrm{M}\because$ Ionic product of $\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2=5.5 \times 10^{-6}$
or, $\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2=\left[\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}\right]+2\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]$
Let, solubility $=S\begin{gathered}\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}+2\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right] \\ S \quad(2 S)^2\end{gathered}$
Also, $K_{\mathrm{sp}}=4 S^3$

$\therefore$ Due to common ion effect,
Molar solubility of $\mathrm{Ca}(\mathrm{OH})_2=\frac{5.5 \times 10^{-6}}{0.1 \times 0.1}=5.5 \times 10^{-4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the $\mathrm{pH}$ of $10 \mathrm{~L}$ of a buffer solution containing $0.01 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ and $0.1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ having $\mathrm{p} K_b$ of 5 ?
questions.solution:
Given, concentration of salt $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}\right)=0.01 \mathrm{M}$
Concentration of base $\left(\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}\right)=0.1 \mathrm{M}\mathrm{p} K_b=5$
A mixture of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ forms basic buffer solution. The Henderson's equation for a basic buffer solution is
$\mathrm{pOH}=\mathrm{p} K_b+\log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Base }]}\mathrm{p} K_b=-\log K_b=-\log 0.1=1$
By substituting values in the above equation, we get
$\mathrm{pOH}=5+\log \frac{0.01}{0.1}=4\mathrm{pH}=14-\mathrm{pOH}=14-4=10$

questions.solution:
Buffer capacity, $\beta=\frac{d C_{\mathrm{HA}}}{d_{\mathrm{pH}}}$,
where, $d C_{\mathrm{HA}}=$ no. of moles of acid added per litre
$\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{pH}} & =\text { change in } \mathrm{pH} \\
d C_{\mathrm{HA}} & =\frac{\text { moles of acetic acid }}{\text { volume }} \\
& =\frac{0.12 / 60}{250 / 1000}=\frac{1}{125} \\
\therefore \quad \beta & =\frac{1 / 125}{0.02}=\frac{1}{2.5}=0.4
\end{aligned}$

\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}^{+}

$\because$ Dissociation occurs $=30 \%$, means 100 moles of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$, gives $=30$ moles of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$-ions.
Thus, 0.1 mole of $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ gives

=\frac{30 \times 0.1}{100}=0.03 \text { mole of } \mathrm{H}^{+} \text {ions. }

$\left(\because\right.$ Concentrating of $\left.\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}=0.1 \mathrm{M}\right)$
Also, $\quad \because \mathrm{pH}=-\mathrm{log}$ [Concentration]

\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{pH}=-\log \left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right] \\
& \mathrm{pH}=-\log [0.03] \\
& \mathrm{pH}=-\log \left[\left(3 \times 10^{-2}\right)\right] \\
& \mathrm{pH}=-0.47+2 \\
& \mathrm{pH}=1.53
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The $p K_a$ of a weak acid is 4.8 . What should be the ratio of $\frac{\text { [acid] }}{\text { [salt }]}$, if a buffer of $\mathrm{pH}=5.8$ is required?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p} K_{\mathrm{a}}+\log \frac{[\text { salt }]}{[\text { acid }]} \\ & 5.8=4.8+\log \frac{\text { [salt }]}{\text { [acid] }} \\ & \therefore \quad \log \frac{\text { [salt }]}{\text { [acid] }}=5.8-4.8=1.0 \\ & \frac{\text { [ salt }]}{\text { [acid }]}=\text { antilog of }[1.0]=\frac{10}{1} \\ & \frac{[\text { acid }]}{[\text { salt }]}=\frac{1}{10}=0.1 \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The $\mathrm{pH}$ of a buffer solution made by mixing $25 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.02 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ and $25 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.2 \mathrm{M}\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ at $25^{\circ}$ is $\left(\mathrm{pK}\right.$ of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}=4.8$ )
questions.solution:
As a mixture of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$ acts as a basic buffer, so its pH must be basic, (i.e., greater than 7), hence the answer must be 2 nd. It can also be find by calculations :

\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{pOH} & =\mathrm{p} K_b+\log \frac{[\text { salt }]}{[\text { base }]} \\
& =4.8+\log \frac{0.2 \mathrm{M}}{0.02 \mathrm{M}} \\
& =4.8 \times \log 10 \\
\mathrm{pOH} & =4.8+1=5.8 \\
\mathrm{pH} & =14-\mathrm{pOH}=14-5.8=8.2
\end{aligned}

questions.solution: A stronger acid will have higher $K_a$ value but smaller $\mathrm{p} K_a$ value while a weaker acid will have smaller $K_a$ value but higher $\mathrm{p} K_a$ value. Hence among the given carboxylic acid the $\mathrm{p} K_a$ value of strongest acid is 0.23 .

questions.q: The correct decreasing order of the basic strength is
questions.solution:
According to the question, Conjugate acids and bases are part of the Bronsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases.

According to this theory, the species that donates a hydrogen cation or proton in a reaction is a conjugate acid, while the remaining portion or the one that accepts a proton or hydrogen is the conjugate base.

The conjugate base may be recognised as an anion.

Conjugated base of weak acid is worked as strong base.

CH3- + H+→CH4 (W.A)CN-+H+→HCNNH2-+H+→NH3HS-+H+ →H2S (S.A)

questions.q: A solution is prepared by mixing $10 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $1.0 \mathrm{M}$ acetic acid and $20 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.5 \mathrm{M}$ sodium acetate and diluted to $100 \mathrm{~mL}$. If the $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ of acetic acid is 4.76 , then the $\mathrm{pH}$ of the solution is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}+\log \frac{[\text { salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]} \\ & {[\text { Acid }]=\left[\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}\right]=\frac{10 \times 1}{100}=0.1 \mathrm{M}} \\ & {[\text { Salt }]=\left[\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COO}^{-}\right]=\frac{20 \times 0.5}{100}=0.1 \mathrm{M}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{pH}=4.76+\log \frac{0.1}{0.1} \\ & =4.76\end{aligned}$
